title: Oct 15 Results + Oct 16 Preview: Split Day, But the Process Holds
summary: Went 1-1 on Oct 15. Tomorrow we're backing the Rays in a bullpen game rematch.

content.value:
## Oct 15 Recap: The Guardians Delivered

Went 1-1 yesterday, which is exactly what happens when you're dealing with tight probability splits. From a pitcher's perspective, the Guardians game played out like we expected—their staff executed when it mattered. The Dodgers miss? That's baseball. Even a 61% confidence pick loses 4 out of 10 times. You can't let one result shake your process.

## What Went Right and Wrong

The **Guardians pick** was never going to be a slam dunk at 52%, but when you're backing the home team with slightly better pitching matchups in October, you take it. They executed.

The **Dodgers miss** stings a bit more at 61% confidence, but let me tell you something from my days on the mound—October baseball is a different animal. Momentum shifts, one bad inning changes everything, and the Brewers showed up. Can't overthink it.

## Oct 16 Preview: Rays @ Guardians Rematch

Here's where it gets interesting. We're flipping the script and backing Tampa Bay tomorrow at 54% confidence. Why? **Nick Martinez** is getting the start for the Rays against **Shawn Armstrong** for Cleveland.

Armstrong as a starter tells me Cleveland is in a bullpen game situation. Martinez has been solid—he's a guy who can give you length and keep hitters off balance with his changeup and cutter mix. When you're facing a bullpen day in the postseason, you want your starter to eat innings and put pressure on their relievers early. Martinez can do that.

content.sub: 54% win probability · Martinez vs Armstrong (bullpen game)

content.value:
## The Pitching Matchup Edge

From a pitcher's perspective, this matchup favors Tampa. Armstrong is a reliever being asked to open—that means Cleveland is piecing together innings. Martinez, on the other hand, is built to go 5-6 innings if his pitch count cooperates.

In October, the team that controls the game early usually controls the bullpen usage late. If Martinez can give Tampa 5 strong, the Rays pen can take over with a lead and short assignments. Cleveland will be mixing and matching from pitch one. That's an edge.

## The Bottom Line

I'm not chasing yesterday's loss. I'm following the process. The 54% confidence isn't screaming certainty, but the pitching setup favors Tampa Bay. When you've got a traditional starter against a bullpen game, and the probabilities are close, I'm taking the team with the defined role on the mound.

Let's get back in the win column tomorrow. Trust the arm, trust the process.
